content.value_statement: Security teams often know their threats but lack a clear path from risk to controls. This skill maps each threat to layered mitigations, coverage gaps, and practical next steps.
actual_capabilities: Maps identified threats to preventive, detective, and corrective controls.
Organizes controls across network, application, data, endpoint, process, and physical layers.
Finds unmapped threats, weak coverage, missing defense in depth, and missing control diversity.
Recommends additional controls from examples such as MFA, WAF, encryption, logging, RBAC, and rate limiting.
Creates mitigation roadmaps, risk reduction summaries, and control effectiveness test reports.
limitations: Does not install, configure, or execute security tools.
Example code requires adaptation before production use.
Control choices still need review against architecture, compliance, budget, and business risk.

use_cases.title: Prioritize Remediation Work
use_cases.description: Convert a threat list into ranked control recommendations and roadmap phases.

use_cases.title: Review Architecture Coverage
use_cases.description: Check whether an application design has layered controls across relevant defense layers.

use_cases.title: Validate Control Effectiveness
use_cases.description: Plan control tests and summarize whether implemented mitigations reduce the intended threats.

prompt_templates.title: Map Basic Threats
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner mapping for a small threat list.
prompt_templates.prompt: Map these threats to security controls. For each threat, include preventive, detective, and corrective options: [paste threat list].

prompt_templates.title: Find Coverage Gaps
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these threats and existing controls. Identify unmapped threats, weak coverage, missing layers, and missing control types: [paste details].

prompt_templates.title: Create a Remediation Roadmap
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning with priority, cost, and timing.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a phased mitigation roadmap from these threats, risks, controls, costs, and constraints. Prioritize critical gaps first: [paste context].

prompt_templates.title: Assess Control Effectiveness
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an effectiveness review for these controls. Include test goals, expected results, evidence needed, and reporting format: [paste controls].

output_examples.input: Threats include account takeover, SQL injection, and data exposure. Existing controls include MFA and TLS.
output: Account takeover has partial coverage from MFA, but needs lockout monitoring and recovery procedures.
SQL injection has no stated mitigation. Add input validation, parameterized queries, WAF rules, and testing.
Data exposure is partly covered by TLS, but needs encryption at rest and access control review.

output_examples.input: A team needs a roadmap for five high-risk application threats with limited budget.
output: Phase 1 addresses critical threats with low coverage and low implementation friction.
Phase 2 adds detective controls and validates control effectiveness.
Phase 3 improves process controls, documentation, and recurring review.

output_examples.input: An architect wants to test whether implemented controls are working.
output: Define one test for each control objective.
Record expected and actual results for each test.
Summarize pass rate, failed controls, and remediation actions.

best_practices: Start with a clear threat list, impact rating, and current control inventory.
Map each threat across multiple layers and control types where practical.
Review mappings regularly because threats, systems, and control effectiveness change.
anti_patterns: Treating one control as complete coverage for a critical threat.
Choosing controls without considering cost, dependencies, and maintenance effort.
Skipping effectiveness testing after a mitigation is implemented.

faq.question: What input does this skill need?
faq.answer: It works best with a threat list, impact ratings, existing controls, constraints, and any compliance requirements.

faq.question: Can it create a threat model?
faq.answer: It can support threat modeling, but its main purpose is mapping known threats to mitigations.

faq.question: Does it execute security tests?
faq.answer: No. It helps design and document control effectiveness tests, but it does not run tools.

faq.question: Which control frameworks does it reference?
faq.answer: The playbook references concepts from NIST Cybersecurity Framework, CIS Controls, MITRE D3FEND, OWASP, and common compliance mappings.

faq.question: Can it help with budget planning?
faq.answer: Yes. The playbook includes examples for prioritizing controls by risk reduction, cost, and roadmap phase.

faq.question: Is this a replacement for security review?
faq.answer: No. Use it to structure analysis, then validate decisions with qualified security and business stakeholders.
